segments.text: Kamrana Razmovar gives another argument: Sussky met Armenians, and in the Bible, as if there are no Armenians at all, that means ancient Armenia is made up.
But the existence of countries and peoples is not established in this way.
Now let’s dispel this myth about Greater Armenia, which included Rusalima.
According to Wikipedia, Greater Armenia existed in the fourth century, then ours is around the fifth.
And somewhere in the middle of these 80 years, I was born in Bethlene, by the way, this is next to Jerusalem. And Sus Christ.
Oddly enough, not a single Arminian met Jesus. There is nothing Armenian in the Bible.
There is no great army, there are dozens of state nationalities and non-ethnics.
But there are no Armenians, no Armin, no need to shove it there, it says “Arorada Mountains.” This is a geographical term.
Ivangelium is not a list of all the peoples of the Middle East. The absence of the people in the story of the life of Christ does not mean their absence in history.
Moreover, the name Arminya is recorded approximately 5 centuries before the birth of Jesus.
Around 520 BC, Darius was the first to leave the Bihistus inscription.
In the Drine Persian text the country is called “Armina of the South of Armenia”.
The Iranica Encyclopedia translates the latter as Armenian.
Now to the statement of the Comran that in the Bible there is armor, but there are no Armenians.
Even this is not true when it comes to Bible translations in general.

In the classic English translation of the King Yaklov Bible, book 4 of TsAS-19, chapter 37 of the element, and in the book “About Rock and Saee”, chapter 37 of the 38th element, the expression land of Armenia is directly used.
In modern translations, the land “Arorad” is more often used in these same places.
And this shows the main problem of the Comran argumate.
Different linguistic and translation traditions can convey ancient geographical names in different ways.
This can be seen even in the Bihistus inscription.
Ancient Persisk versions use the name Armin o Vavilovskaya Uroshtu,
that is, the old Mesaputan name "Urartu" existed early in the same region.
There is independent Greek evidence.
Herodotus from the fifth century BC mentions Armenians.
